title: The Last Leaf
focus: hope created by an act of sacrifice

teacherSummary.text: In Greenwich Village, young artist Johnsy is dying of pneumonia and believes she will die when the last ivy leaf falls outside her window. Her friend Sue tells their neighbor, the old failed painter Behrman. Through a stormy night one leaf survives, and Johnsy regains her will to live. Then they learn Behrman died of pneumonia after painting the leaf on the wall in the storm: his masterpiece.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “When the last one falls I must go, too” slowly and put it in my own words: Johnsy, sick with pneumonia, tells Sue she will die when the last leaf falls. Next, craft. I notice she ties her life to the leaf, which shows she has given up. The strongest word is “falls”: it shows a quiet, inevitable motion. Then, effect. Why does Johnsy believe she will die when the last leaf falls? My answer: Johnsy believes she will die when the last leaf falls because her illness has made her lose the will to live; the story will show how hope, and Behrman's sacrifice, change that.
